edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 42,500,000 for the Shares, payable in immediately available funds at Closing.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur within 45 days after signing, subject to satisfaction or waiver of the conditions set forth in this Agreement, or on such other date as the parties may agree in writing.

3. Seller Representations. The Seller represents and warrants to the Buyer that: (a) the Seller has good and valid title to the Shares, free and clear of liens other than transfer restrictions arising under applicable securities laws; (b) the Seller has full authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (c) the capitalization of the Company is as set forth in the disclosure schedules; (d) the financial statements delivered to Buyer have been prepared in accordance with the Company’s past practices and fairly present in all material respects the financial condition and results of operations of the Company for the periods presented; (e) except as disclosed in the disclosure schedules, the Company has no material undisclosed liabilities other than liabilities incurred in the ordinary course of business since the date of the most recent financial statements; (f) the Company is in compliance in all material respects with applicable laws; (g) the Company has filed all material tax returns required to be filed and has paid all material taxes due, except those being contested in good faith; (h) the material contracts of the Company are listed in the disclosure schedules and are in full force and effect in all material respects; (i) there is no material litigation pending or, to Seller’s knowledge, threatened against the Company; (j) the Company is in material compliance with applicable employment and employee benefit laws; (k) except as disclosed in the disclosure schedules, no material third-party consent is required for Seller’s execution or performance of this Agreement; and (l) since the date of the most recent financial statements, there has not been a Material Adverse Effect.

4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement are confidential; provided that either party may disclose such terms to its legal, tax, accounting, financial, financing, regulatory, and other professional advisors, prospective financing sources, and governmental authorities, in each case to the extent reasonably necessary and subject to customary confidentiality obligations or legal requirements.

5. Closing Conditions. Buyer’s obligation to consummate the Closing is subject to: (a) the Seller representations being true and correct in all material respects as of Closing, except that representations qualified by materiality shall be true and correct in all respects; (b) Seller having performed in all material respects its covenants required to be performed before Closing; (c) receipt of required material third-party and regulatory consents, if any, set forth in the disclosure schedules; (d) no Material Adverse Effect having occurred after signing; and (e) completion of Buyer’s confirmatory due diligence, provided that such diligence condition shall be deemed satisfied unless Buyer provides written notice of a specific material diligence objection within 20 days after signing. Seller’s obligation to consummate the Closing is subject to Buyer having delivered the Purchase Price and performed in all material respects its covenants required to be performed before Closing.

6. Interim Operating Covenants. From signing until Closing, except as required by law, expressly contemplated by this Agreement, disclosed in the disclosure schedules, or approved by Buyer in writing, Seller shall cause the Company to conduct its business in the ordinary course in all material respects and shall not cause the Company to take any material non-ordinary-course action, including amending organizational documents, issuing equity securities, incurring material indebtedness outside the ordinary course, selling material assets outside the ordinary course, entering into or terminating material contracts outside the ordinary course, making material changes to employee compensation or benefit arrangements outside the ordinary course, or settling material litigation.

7. Indemnification. Following Closing, Seller shall indemnify Buyer for losses arising from breaches of Seller representations, breaches of Seller covenants, and pre-Closing taxes of the Company, subject to customary limitations, including: (a) no indemnification for representation breaches unless aggregate recoverable losses exceed USD 425,000, after which only amounts in excess of such threshold shall be recoverable; (b) an aggregate cap for representation breach claims equal to 10% of the Purchase Price, except for fraud, willful misconduct, title to Shares, authority, and tax matters; (c) survival of general representations for 18 months after Closing, and survival of fundamental and tax representations until 60 days after expiration of the applicable statute of limitations; and (d) Buyer’s obligation to use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate losses and pursue available insurance or third-party recoveries.

receiver.message_back:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for the revised draft. Seller’s movement is helpful, and Buyer is prepared to move forward promptly if the remaining commercial and protection points can be resolved.

On price, Buyer can proceed at USD 40,000,000, subject to final agreement on the documentation and schedules. The revised draft still leaves Buyer assuming meaningful diligence and post-Closing risk, particularly given the financial-statement formulation, undisclosed-liability language, and indemnity limitations. If Seller is seeking a rapid signing on a 45-day Closing timeline, Buyer will need the price to reflect those residual risks.

In addition, please revise the draft to include the following:

1. Financial Statements. The financial statement representation should state that the financial statements were prepared in accordance with GAAP, consistently applied, and fairly present in all material respects the Company’s financial condition and results of operations for the periods presented.

2. Undisclosed Liabilities. The no-undisclosed-liabilities representation should cover all material liabilities other than those reflected or reserved in the financial statements or expressly disclosed in the schedules.

3. Closing Bring-Down. Seller’s representations should be true and correct at Closing, with fundamental representations true in all respects and other representations true except where the failure to be true would not reasonably be expected to be material.

4. Indemnity Basket. The basket should be reduced to USD 300,000 and operate as a tipping basket, so once the threshold is exceeded, Buyer may recover losses from the first dollar.

5. Indemnity Cap. The cap for general representation breaches should be increased to 15% of the Purchase Price. Fundamental, tax, fraud, willful misconduct, title, and authority claims should remain uncapped or separately addressed outside the general cap.

6. Escrow. Ten percent of the Purchase Price should be placed in escrow for 18 months to support Seller’s indemnity obligations.

7. Mitigation / Third-Party Recoveries. Buyer can agree to a commercially reasonable mitigation obligation, but Buyer should not be required to pursue insurance or third-party recoveries as a condition to recovery from Seller. Seller may receive appropriate subrogation rights after payment.

8. Interim Covenants. Please add customary interim operating covenants restricting non-ordinary-course actions, distributions, new indebtedness, compensation changes, material contract amendments, and related-party transactions without Buyer’s prior consent.

Subject to these changes, Buyer is prepared to work toward prompt finalization.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP
Counsel for Buyer
